 RILS 2021: Innovation in Educational Assessment Systems 4

Why focus on Innovation in an Assessment Systems?
• Assessment systems are often seen as burdensome and of little use by
 stakeholders.
• Assessment is considered an essential lynchpin for effective education.
• Social and economic pressures to raise student educational attainment
• Ensure greater equity of educational outcomes for all students
• Assessment is essential component to effectively educating students
• Assessment (it is believed) has not yet fulfilled its promise
 • Rapidly advancing technologies can allow for use of simulations, interactivity, and
 collaboration
 • Need to motivate and engage students
 • Signal changes for curriculum and instruction, such as inclusion of 21st century skills

Design Innovation
 Innovation includes:
 Desirability - the quality of being
 wanted;
 Feasibility - the possibility, capability, or
 likelihood of something being done or
 accomplished, and viability; and
 Viability – ability to work as intended
 and succeed.

 In other words, Design innovation is a
 process that leads to innovation.

 There is no one process for innovating.

 RILS 2021: Innovation in Educational Assessment Systems 15

Design Innovation: Human Centered Design
Design Innovation of an assessment system assumes:
• A basic knowledge of the characteristics of the system, including:
 • Areas of strength
 • Areas of need
 • Culture of individuals in the system
• A profound knowledge of the system, including:
 • Build shared ownership of improvement
 • Detect and learn from variations in practice
 • Build and share knowledge among practitioners
 • Motivate users and innovators
